answer: Data availability sampling lets light clients check that a block's data is really published by downloading only a few random pieces, relying on erasure coding so any small sample implies the whole block can be reconstructed. A violet shard sampled at random stands in for the whole, a knoll of sampled pieces from many clients together covers the block, and a bridge of coded redundancy connects the samples to the full data. A farm cannot hide most of a block while serving a few samples, because random sampling across many clients will hit the missing pieces.
